disposition_boundary: All requirements are POST_CANARY/R5 and do not alter R4.1 READY_FOR_CANARY.

requirements.title: Exclusive recovery ownership and fencing
requirements.invariant: Exactly one current lease holder may advance an operation; every send and state mutation is conditioned on a monotonically increasing fence token, and superseded owners are inert.
requirements.positive_fixture: Two workers contend; one obtains fence N and alone advances the operation.
requirements.negative_fixture: A worker using expired fence N-1 attempts send and ACK after fence N is committed.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Pause the owner at each pre-send and pre-ACK boundary, expire its lease, transfer ownership, then resume it under skewed wall clocks.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: For every operation, accepted mutations have one strictly monotonic fence lineage and network_send_count_by_nonmax_fence equals zero.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Lease/fence acquisition and conditional mutation APIs only; no distributed topology support yet.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback must reject rows written with an unknown newer fence schema and must never revive an expired owner.
requirements.research_relevance: Tests whether database-backed fencing is sufficient for local multiprocess recovery under adversarial scheduling.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G01 passes every scheduled takeover point with one authority and zero stale-owner effects.

requirements.title: Authenticated request-bound receipts
requirements.invariant: ACKED is reachable only from a receipt cryptographically binding issuer, trust epoch, protocol version, project, operation, canonical request digest, event identity, and outcome.
requirements.positive_fixture: A canonical receipt signed by the authorized current-epoch key matches every pending-request binding.
requirements.negative_fixture: A structurally valid receipt has a mismatched project or operation identifier.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Mutate each signed field, signature byte, key ID, trust epoch, canonicalization form, and replay context independently and in pairs.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Only the unmodified authorized vector verifies; every mutation returns a stable reason code and leaves the outbox non-ACKED.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Receipt envelope, canonicalization, trust-store lookup, and verification; excludes recovery policy.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback must retain verification material for already persisted receipts and fail closed on newer receipt versions.
requirements.research_relevance: Defines the trust boundary required to turn transport-authenticated JSON into durable protocol evidence.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G02 accepts all authorized positives and rejects the complete mutation corpus with zero false ACKs.

requirements.title: Explicit durable reconciliation state machine
requirements.invariant: Each operation follows a versioned durable transition graph; ambiguity is represented as INDETERMINATE and can never be collapsed into success or automatic retransmission.
requirements.positive_fixture: QUEUED to SENDING to INDETERMINATE to RECONCILING to ACKED using a verified receipt.
requirements.negative_fixture: An illegal ACKED-to-SENDING or INDETERMINATE-to-ACKED transition without verified receipt evidence.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Crash immediately before and after every state write and network action, then replay each resulting database image.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: The observed transition sequence is accepted by the frozen graph and every restart converges to its model-predicted state without an unauthorized send.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Local durable state representation and transition validation; excludes retention and distributed authority.
requirements.rollback_implications: Migration must be reversible for states understood by the prior version; unknown or lossy states block rollback.
requirements.research_relevance: Makes ambiguity explicit enough for model-based crash exploration and later distributed refinement.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G03 covers every declared transition boundary with no model divergence or implicit resend.

requirements.title: Malformed and cross-bound receipt handling
requirements.invariant: A receipt is valid atomically or causes no ACK and no destructive state change; all request and event bindings must match the pending record.
requirements.positive_fixture: A size-bounded canonical receipt exactly matches its pending record and signature.
requirements.negative_fixture: A required field is missing or has the wrong JSON type.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Apply the versioned receipt corpus at HTTP, parser, database-load, and restart boundaries with chunking and size-limit edges.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Each vector maps to one frozen reason code and expected INDETERMINATE or QUARANTINED state; false_ack_count is zero.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Bounded parsing and semantic validation only; hostile bytes are never interpolated into unbounded logs.
requirements.rollback_implications: Older parsers must reject unsupported envelopes without rewriting or deleting them.
requirements.research_relevance: Measures fail-closed behavior at the syntax-to-authority seam.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G04 produces deterministic classifications for every vector with zero false ACKs and bounded resource use.

requirements.title: Crash-safe local ACK persistence
requirements.invariant: A crash during ACK persistence recovers to the prior reconcilable state or one fully durable verified ACK, never a torn, false, or unrecoverable state.
requirements.positive_fixture: Verified receipt and ACK row commit atomically with the current fence.
requirements.negative_fixture: Receipt bytes persist but the ACK transition does not commit.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Inject kill and I/O failure at each SQLite transaction, WAL, checkpoint, and fsync boundary while a stale owner races.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: SQLite integrity passes and recovered state is exactly pre-transaction or fully committed; receipt re-verifies and no extra network effect occurs.
requirements.implementation_boundary: ACK transaction and restart recovery only; excludes generic corruption repair.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback requires a proven reader for committed ACK records and must preserve indeterminate records byte-for-byte.
requirements.research_relevance: Closes the untested local durability window between verified receipt and durable acknowledgment.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G05 passes every declared persistence crash point under both current and stale fences.

requirements.title: Corruption quarantine and recoverability
requirements.invariant: Corruption causes no send, ACK, deletion, or silent repair; the smallest provably safe unit is quarantined and original bytes are retained.
requirements.positive_fixture: A valid outbox passes integrity checks and resumes unaffected operations.
requirements.negative_fixture: One operation payload digest is invalid and is quarantined without affecting a valid neighbor.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Apply reproducible page, WAL, schema, JSON, digest, and receipt mutations singly and in combinations to copied databases.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Network action count remains zero for corrupt units; quarantine scope matches the corpus expectation and forensic hashes match input bytes.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Detection, quarantine, and operator export; no automatic repair.
requirements.rollback_implications: Quarantine metadata must survive downgrade or force rollback refusal; forensic originals are immutable.
requirements.research_relevance: Tests whether partial progress can coexist with strict corruption containment.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G06 classifies the full corruption corpus without unsafe action or evidence loss.

requirements.title: Disk exhaustion and persistence error semantics
requirements.invariant: No send starts without committed pre-send state and no ACK is reported without a durable verified receipt; storage failure is visible and bounded.
requirements.positive_fixture: Operations persist and recover normally within declared storage headroom.
requirements.negative_fixture: Enqueue encounters SQLite FULL before any network action.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Exhaust bytes and inodes or inject persistence errors at enqueue, transition, receipt, ACK, evidence, and log boundaries.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: No unjournaled external action or false success occurs; after capacity restoration, state matches the predicted safe checkpoint.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Persistence error classification and bounded reporting; excludes infrastructure auto-scaling.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback is prohibited while durability health is unknown and must not consume reserved recovery space.
requirements.research_relevance: Separates durable protocol safety from host storage liveness.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G07 passes all storage-failure boundaries and successful bounded restoration cases.

requirements.title: Stale-operation policy and explicit operator disposition
requirements.invariant: Age never implies absence, resend, success, or deletion; stale and indeterminate operations remain queryable until a versioned authorized disposition is durable.
requirements.positive_fixture: An authorized reconcile disposition records actor, policy version, reason, and resulting state.
requirements.negative_fixture: An operation crosses max age with no authorization and remains unchanged and queryable.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Cross age boundaries under clock anomalies while racing inspect, reconcile, cancel, resume, and delayed receipt arrival.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Final state is derived solely from monotonic duration plus authenticated disposition/receipt inputs, never wall-clock age alone.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Policy engine and audited operator commands; excludes automatic destructive expiry.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback must preserve operator dispositions and cannot reinterpret newer policy outcomes.
requirements.research_relevance: Studies human authority at the boundary where protocol knowledge is irreducibly incomplete.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G08 proves all stale actions are explicit, authenticated, durable, and replay-stable.

requirements.title: Multi-process and multi-host recovery contract
requirements.invariant: Each supported topology has a qualified lease authority with fencing; unsupported topology fails closed before send.
requirements.positive_fixture: Declared multiprocess topology elects one fenced authority and converges after failover.
requirements.negative_fixture: An undeclared shared-filesystem multi-host topology is rejected before opening recovery.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Partition lease and Station paths independently, reboot nodes, and resume stale replicas across every takeover point.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Each schedule yields one fenced advancement lineage or an explicit unsupported result, with no second receiver effect.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Topology declaration and lease adapter contract; excludes receipt replication semantics.
requirements.rollback_implications: Topology downgrade requires draining owners and proving no newer lease epoch remains active.
requirements.research_relevance: Determines where SQLite-local safety ends and distributed authority becomes mandatory.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G09 passes every supported topology and rejects every unsupported topology without effects.

requirements.title: Reconciliation observability and SLO metrics
requirements.invariant: Every durable transition emits one correlation-safe observation; bounded-cardinality metrics reconcile to durable state without secret or message disclosure.
requirements.positive_fixture: A mixed workload emits one reason-coded observation per committed transition and reconciled aggregate counts.
requirements.negative_fixture: Exporter outage leaves protocol state correct and later exposes a detectable observation gap.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Inject hostile identifiers, receipt bodies, high-cardinality values, duplicated export, dropped export, and skewed clocks.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Recomputed journal counters equal accepted telemetry plus explicit gap records; label sets stay within frozen bounds and redaction corpus leaks zero tokens.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Structured events, metrics, redaction, and alerts; telemetry cannot authorize protocol transitions.
requirements.rollback_implications: Metric schema changes need compatibility aliases; rollback must not erase audit observations.
requirements.research_relevance: Tests whether operational visibility can remain complete enough without increasing confidentiality or control-plane risk.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G10 reconciles all scenarios with bounded labels, zero leakage, and deterministic stuck-state alerts.

requirements.title: Protocol versioning and compatibility negotiation
requirements.invariant: Sender, Station, stored request, and receipt negotiate compatible versions and safety features before mutation; unknown majors and safety-removing downgrades fail closed.
requirements.positive_fixture: Two supported minor versions negotiate the required receipt-binding feature set.
requirements.negative_fixture: An unknown major version produces no persistent or external effect.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Exercise upgrade, downgrade, restart, and rollback across the pairwise version matrix while stripping or duplicating feature offers.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Negotiated version equals the matrix result; incompatible pairs have zero state and network effects beyond bounded negotiation.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Envelope versions and feature negotiation; excludes feature implementations beyond required safety flags.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback is allowed only where the compatibility matrix proves older code can safely read persisted rows and receipts.
requirements.research_relevance: Provides a controlled evolution surface for every later R5 invariant.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G11 passes the full supported matrix and all incompatible/downgrade cases fail closed.

requirements.title: Distributed receipt lookup authority and consistency
requirements.invariant: NOT_FOUND, NOT_AUTHORITATIVE, and INDETERMINATE are distinct; only an authority-backed answer may advance state, and absence never authorizes duplicate effect.
requirements.positive_fixture: The authoritative leader returns a bound positive receipt that advances reconciliation.
requirements.negative_fixture: A lagging replica returns NOT_AUTHORITATIVE and causes no retransmission.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Enumerate lag, failover, partition, stale-cache, lost-index, and DR schedules with delayed positive receipts.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: State follows the frozen authority model and receiver effect cardinality never exceeds one across all schedules.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Lookup authority and response semantics; excludes general-purpose consensus implementation claims.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback must maintain authoritative-read semantics or suspend reconciliation.
requirements.research_relevance: Tests the knowledge limits of negative answers in replicated receipt stores.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G12 converges under every declared schedule without absence-driven repost.

requirements.title: Receipt retention, tombstones, and garbage collection
requirements.invariant: GC preserves authenticated uniqueness evidence for at least the maximum replay horizon; deletion cannot make an old operation appear new.
requirements.positive_fixture: Expired full receipt becomes a compact authenticated tombstone while uniqueness lookup remains authoritative.
requirements.negative_fixture: A GC request inside the replay horizon is rejected and leaves the receipt intact.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Race GC with lookup and recovery, restore snapshots from before GC, shrink policy, and apply storage pressure at boundary times.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: No schedule produces a second receiver effect; retained proof covers the declared horizon and storage growth respects its bound.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Receipt/tombstone lifecycle only; message-content deletion policy remains separately governed.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback must understand tombstones or disable sends for operations whose uniqueness proof it cannot read.
requirements.research_relevance: Explores bounded storage without weakening temporal idempotency claims.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G13 passes all boundary/race/restore cases with one effect and bounded retained storage.

requirements.title: Formal at-most-once external-effect claim boundary
requirements.invariant: Published at-most-once claims stop at the proven boundary; downstream effects require a globally stable effect ID and transactional or idempotent consumption, otherwise outcome is INDETERMINATE.
requirements.positive_fixture: An idempotent consumer commits one effect for repeated delivery of one stable effect ID.
requirements.negative_fixture: A non-idempotent connector is classified outside the at-most-once claim and cannot produce a success attestation.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Explore every producer, broker, consumer, effect, and ACK crash boundary with duplicate/reordered delivery and snapshot restore.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: The executable model and implementation trace refinement satisfy the scoped safety property or retain a minimal counterexample.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Claim definition, stable effect identity, and reference consumer contract; no claim for arbitrary downstream systems.
requirements.rollback_implications: Rollback cannot broaden claims and must preserve stable effect identities across version changes.
requirements.research_relevance: Establishes the precise theorem supported by the protocol rather than relying on informal exactly-once language.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G14 exhausts the bounded model, passes refinement traces, and publishes the exact supported claim boundary.

requirements.title: Evidence provenance, completeness, and retention governance
requirements.invariant: Every qualification result is bound to immutable source, harness, corpus, environment, and authorization identities; missing, skipped, malformed, overwritten, or unverifiable evidence cannot pass.
requirements.positive_fixture: A complete sealed run contains all declared gate artifacts, provenance, authorization, and matching hashes.
requirements.negative_fixture: One required artifact is absent or hash-mismatched.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Mutate manifests, paths, timestamps, candidate IDs, corpus IDs, duplicate entries, symlinks, and prior-failure retention records.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Canonical manifest verification returns PASS only for the complete authorized set and stable reason-coded failure otherwise.
requirements.implementation_boundary: External qualification evidence tooling only; never candidate runtime code or authoritative evidence mutation.
requirements.rollback_implications: Evidence schemas remain readable for the retention period; migrations create new records rather than rewriting sealed evidence.
requirements.research_relevance: Makes experimental reproducibility and negative-result retention enforceable rather than procedural.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G15 passes positive evidence and rejects every completeness/provenance mutation.

requirements.title: Deterministic fault orchestration and corpus registry
requirements.invariant: A named seed, schedule, corpus revision, and fault point reproduce the same actions, oracle result, and evidence digest independent of test order.
requirements.positive_fixture: Two isolated executions of one schedule produce identical canonical traces and decisions.
requirements.negative_fixture: An unknown fault point or corpus digest is rejected before execution.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Permute test order, CPU count, locale, timezone, hash seed, and injected scheduling yields while holding the logical schedule fixed.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Canonical action traces, decisions, and manifests are byte-identical except explicitly normalized environment fields.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Test harness, model, and fixture registry only; no runtime feature implementation.
requirements.rollback_implications: Harness revisions are immutable and prior corpus/fault identifiers remain resolvable.
requirements.research_relevance: Enables reproducible counterexamples for concurrency and crash research.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G16 reproduces every reference schedule twice with identical normalized evidence.

requirements.title: Independent phase convergence and release qualification
requirements.invariant: Each phase is independently pinned, qualified, rollback-tested, and reviewed before dependents begin; final convergence consumes immutable phase receipts and reruns cross-phase safety tests.
requirements.positive_fixture: Six immutable phase receipts form one dependency-complete release manifest and the cross-phase suite passes.
requirements.negative_fixture: A missing, stale, or wrong-tree phase receipt blocks convergence.
requirements.adversarial_fixture: Substitute receipts, reorder phases, remove gates, drift one corpus, and attempt partial rollback across schema boundaries.
requirements.deterministic_oracle: Topological validation and manifest verification accept exactly the declared phase closure; all cross-phase invariants pass on one release tree.
requirements.implementation_boundary: Release qualification and governance only; it cannot merge, deploy, or promote.
requirements.rollback_implications: Every phase supplies a tested rollback boundary; final release blocks when any dependency edge lacks one.
requirements.research_relevance: Tests whether evidence can compose across independently reviewed increments without laundering stale claims.
requirements.exit_criteria: R5-G17 verifies all phase receipts and the final cross-phase suite with no missing or weakened gate.
